explanation:
I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. `quotientInfRingEquivPiQuotientOfPairwiseSupEqTop` is defined by the library itself (Finite.lean, line 115). It is the Chinese remainder ring isomorphism for two-sided ideals in a ring that need not be commutative, with pairwise `I i ⊔ I j = ⊤`. The theorem only says that the inverse of this isomorphism sends `fun i => mk (I i) r` back to `mk (⨅ i, I i) r`. The proof is `RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply`, a general fact about any equivalence, so the substance lies in the library's own definition.

The closest Mathlib declaration is `Ideal.quotientInfRingEquivPiQuotient` in RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean. It needs `CommRing R` and `Pairwise (IsCoprime on f)`, so it does not apply in this setting. A grep of Mathlib's `Mathlib/` sources found only that equivalence and the `quotientInfToPiQuotient_*` lemmas (`_mk`, `_mk'`, `_inj`, `_surj`); there is no `_symm_mk` lemma, even for the commutative version.
